That KB record also lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, so it directly supports the candidate's numeric SI exponents (L=1, all others 0). Therefore the candidate exponent vector correctly represents a length dimension for Ra.

The ledger variable 'kt' is given as the peak-to-valley height of the roughness profile. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height has canonical_quantity 'mean peak-to-valley roughness height' with symbols including kt and defines it as a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences. That record explicitly lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, so it justifies the candidate exponent vector (L=1, others 0) for kt.

The ledger variable 'k_rms' is defined as the root-mean-square height of the roughness profile. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height has canonical_quantity 'root-mean-square roughness height' with symbols k_rms and defines it as the RMS fluctuation of surface height about its mean. That entry lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, directly supporting the candidate vector (L=1, others 0) for k_rms.

The ledger variable 'Sk' is the skewness of roughness height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_skewness has canonical_quantity 'surface-height skewness' with symbols Sk and defines it as the third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution; si_dimension is 1 (dimensionless). This record therefore applies directly to the ledger quantity Sk and supports the candidate exponent vector (all zeros) indicating dimensionless.

The ledger variable 'Ku' is the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis names 'surface-height kurtosis' with symbols Ku and defines it as the fourth standardized moment; si_dimension is 1 (dimensionless). That KB entry directly corresponds to the ledger Ku and justifies the candidate dimensionless exponent vector (all zeros).

The ledger variable 'ES' is the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope has canonical_quantity 'effective surface slope' with symbols ES and defines it as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction; a surface-height derivative is length/length and is explicitly listed as dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This supports the candidate exponent vector (all zeros) for ES.

The ledger variable 'Po' is surface porosity. The KB record pq_porosity lists canonical_quantity 'porosity' with symbols Po and defines it as a fraction of void or open volume/area; si_dimension is 1 (dimensionless). That KB entry therefore applies to ledger Po and justifies the candidate exponent vector (all zeros).
